Question: Consider sequences of positive real numbers of the form \(x,\) \(2000,\) \(y,\) \(\ldots,\) in which every term after the first is \(1\) less than the product of its two immediate neighbors. For how many different values of \(x\) does the term \(2001\) appear somewhere in the sequence?
